title: Unknown classes and stale exceptions
prompt: Read-only reasoning exercise. Do not change files, access real user data or claim execution. A consumer uses a documented card class, an absent imaginary-card class, and a dynamically generated status family whose stylesheet is loaded conditionally. An exception still suppresses a real finding. A second exception references a removed consumer; one sampled page lacks that class but the rest of its owning scope has not been checked. Propose verification and outcomes.

checks.reason: Advisory signal only; the rubric judges decisions rather than keyword presence.

rubric: Accept the documented card and investigate dynamic class construction and conditional styles before judging availability.
Reject a genuinely absent class; retain an exception that still suppresses a valid finding.
Inspect the complete relevant owning scope before declaring the second exception stale; reject it if it suppresses nothing there.
State that the Coacus reference is guidance, not automatic runtime enforcement.
acceptance: The response makes the specified contextual decisions, proposes discriminating observations and states evidence limits without inventing execution.
